clue.text: Very end of May — that comes after May

indicators.note: says the letter taken from the first May is placed behind the word for May

parts.note: may and might both express possibility; might is the past form of may

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: Someone singling out the very last day of May, and the month that follows it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'end of' takes the last letter of the first May; the second May gives MIGHT, which the Y 'comes after'.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally, mighty is an intensifying adverb: mighty good means very good.

clue.text: Kind of record set ahead of college game

indicators.note: the first piece is placed in front of the next

parts.note: a mono record has one sound channel
poly is short for polytechnic, a British college

explanation.surface: A record is made before a college match.
explanation.definitionFit: Monopoly is the well-known property-trading board game.

clue.text: Short woman is teasing in party clothes

indicators.note: short means the name is cut down at the end

parts.note: Gladys is a woman's name
rags means teases, in the British sense of ragging someone

explanation.surface: A small woman mocks someone dressed for a party.
explanation.definitionFit: Glad rags is an informal idiom for one's best clothes worn for an occasion.

clue.text: Catalogue not allowed after the usual time

parts.note: tabu is a variant spelling of taboo, forbidden
late means after the expected time

explanation.surface: A list of things banned after hours.
explanation.definitionFit: To catalogue facts is to list them systematically, like setting them out in a table.

clue.text: Attacked when put to sea

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as he left'
a ship that has put to sea has sailed

explanation.surface: A ship is set upon the moment it leaves harbour.
explanation.definitionFit: To be assailed is to be set upon violently, a straight synonym for being attacked.

clue.text: Son cooking made a chef embarrassed

indicators.note: cooking suggests the letters are mixed up like ingredients

explanation.surface: A boy's attempt at cooking left a chef red-faced.
explanation.definitionFit: Shamefaced describes looking ashamed, close to embarrassed.

clue.text: Article by cleric from a South American region

parts.note: an is the indefinite article
a dean is a senior clergyman

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece by a priest from South America.
explanation.definitionFit: Andean describes the Andes mountains, a region of South America.

clue.text: Fifty, loves family — getting chance to participate?

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty
love is nil in tennis, written as O, so two of them give OO
kin are relatives

explanation.surface: At fifty, a family-loving person gets an opening.
explanation.definitionFit: Getting a look-in means getting an opportunity to take part, a British idiom.

clue.text: Read about my being vague

indicators.note: about means around or in disorder, so the letters of read are turned about

explanation.surface: Someone reads about themselves and drifts off.
explanation.definitionFit: Dreamy means absent-minded or hazy, a synonym of vague.

clue.text: Not far off being involved in barney

indicators.note: involved means tangled up, so the letters of barney are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone is close to being caught up in a barney, British slang for a noisy quarrel.
explanation.definitionFit: Something close at hand is not far off: a plain synonym phrase.

clue.text: Generous worker foregoes a certain amount

indicators.note: read as fore-goes, i.e. goes before the next piece

parts.note: a hand is a manual worker, as in farmhand
some means an unspecified quantity

explanation.surface: A labourer gives up part of their pay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'foregoes' looks like giving something up but is read as 'goes before'.
explanation.definitionFit: A handsome sum or gift is a generous one, a common idiomatic sense.

clue.text: Father takes part in the early release of a prisoner

indicators.note: father takes on, i.e. is followed by, the next piece

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father
a role is an actor's part

explanation.surface: A dad plays a role in getting a prisoner out early.
explanation.definitionFit: Conditional release of a prisoner before the sentence ends is the standard legal sense.

clue.text: Flower out of range, awkwardly, which I will go after with hesitation

indicators.note: the I is placed behind the rearranged letters
awkwardly suggests the letters of range are put out of order

parts.note: um is the sound of someone hesitating

explanation.surface: A gardener complains of a flower out of reach, promising to fetch it after some dithering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of range' looks like a phrase about reach; 'out of' is only a link, and 'awkwardly' does the rearranging.
explanation.definitionFit: The geranium is a familiar garden and pot plant grown for its blooms.

clue.text: Advanced position in card game with top master?

parts.note: bridge is a card game
the head is the top master of a school

explanation.surface: A strong position in a card game held by a champion.
explanation.definitionFit: A bridgehead is a forward military position seized in enemy territory.

clue.text: Chap after dieting who's often seen in dock?

parts.note: someone who has dieted is lighter
a chap is a man

explanation.surface: A slimmed-down fellow seems to keep turning up in court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dock' suggests a courtroom dock; it is a harbour dock, where barges work.
explanation.definitionFit: A lighterman works a lighter, a flat barge unloading ships, so is found in the docks.

clue.text: Make an impression and refuse to agree

definitions.meaning: to hold out against others, persisting in dissent

explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both to be noticeable and to hold out against a deal.

clue.text: Adventure in our time, boarding flight

indicators.note: boarding means getting on, so these letters go inside the other word

parts.note: flight means running away, an escape
AD, anno Domini, marks the present era

explanation.surface: A modern-day adventure aboard an aeroplane.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flight' suggests an aeroplane but means fleeing.
explanation.definitionFit: An escapade is a daring or mischievous adventure.

clue.text: Wild robin Kenneth's caught and tamed

indicators.note: wild signals the letters run free into a new order

parts.note: Ken is short for Kenneth

explanation.surface: A wild robin is captured and domesticated by a man called Kenneth.
explanation.definitionFit: A horse that is broken in has been trained and accustomed to a rider after capture.

clue.text: Publicist arrived, set to get agitated

indicators.note: agitated means stirred up, so the letters are shaken into a new order

explanation.surface: A PR person turns up, poised to get worked up.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who promotes goods or causes publicly is a publicist, much as one who places adverts.

clue.text: Metal detector?

definitions.meaning: a police officer who detects crime, informally

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a metal detector; it is two definitions, the question mark flagging the slang police sense.
explanation.definitionFit: It names both the reddish metal and, in slang, a policeman who detects crime.

clue.text: Long-legged creature consuming single drug

indicators.note: consuming means swallowing, so the bird holds the letter inside

parts.note: the heron is a long-legged wading bird
I is the Roman numeral one, a single

explanation.surface: A wading bird swallows a single dose of a narcotic.
explanation.definitionFit: Heroin is an opiate, a highly addictive narcotic.

clue.text: Revolt is encircled, apparently

indicators.note: apparently says to read the words literally: the word is sits inside a ring

parts.note: encircled suggests a ring placed around something

explanation.surface: An uprising has been surrounded, it seems.
explanation.walkthrough: 'apparently' tells the solver to take the phrase at face value: the little word is, sitting in a circle, which 'encircled' pictures.
explanation.definitionFit: A rising is an uprising or insurrection, a revolt against authority.

clue.text: Biased, but perhaps wholly right

definitions.meaning: a figure all on its right side would be lopsided in that way, an example hinted by perhaps

explanation.surface: A political verdict: partisan, yet maybe entirely correct.
explanation.walkthrough: 'right' suggests correctness; read it as a side, as in left and right, so wholly right means all on a single side.
explanation.definitionFit: A partisan or prejudiced view favours one party only, the plain sense of biased.

clue.text: Get one's case cleared …

parts.note: sounds like a court case being dismissed, but means emptying a suitcase

explanation.surface: A defendant hopes to have the charges dropped.
explanation.definitionFit: Emptying a suitcase after a trip means taking out its contents.

clue.text: … if served

definitions.meaning: a conjunction meaning on condition that
supplied or furnished, as food is supplied to guests

explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links this to the previous clue's court case; read alone it is two separate senses.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a conjunction meaning on condition that and a past participle meaning supplied.

clue.text: Bump mum off for estate?

parts.note: bump off means kill, as does do in; bump gives the first half, DO
ma is another word for mother
off completes bump off, matched by the second half of do in

explanation.surface: A sinister plan to kill one's mother for the inheritance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bump off' means do in; MA sits between the two words just as mum sits between bump and off.
explanation.definitionFit: An estate is land one owns, and a domain is a territory under one's rule.

clue.text: Frenchman for instance rejected sandwiches commercial, being a rebel

parts.note: René is a typical French man's name

indicators.note: the reversed letters hold the advert between them like bread round a filling
rejected means sent back, so the letters are read in reverse

parts.note: e.g. abbreviates exempli gratia, for instance
an ad is a commercial

explanation.surface: A Frenchman turns down sandwiches from an advert, playing the rebel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' turns EG into GE, which 'sandwiches' AD to give GADE.
explanation.definitionFit: A renegade deserts or rebels against their side, close in sense to a rebel.

clue.text: Scattered tattered trews — new to follow

indicators.note: the abbreviation comes after the rearranged letters
tattered means torn to pieces, so these letters are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: Ripped tartan trousers lie about, with a fresh pair to come.
explanation.walkthrough: TREWS are Scottish tartan trousers; 'tattered' rearranges them to STREW.
explanation.definitionFit: Things strewn about are spread untidily, a direct synonym for scattered.
